subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about an electric motor:

(a) It uses a commutator that reverses the direction of the current in the coil after each half-rotation.

(b) The direction of the force on an arm of the coil can be found using Fleming's left-hand rule.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is **Both (a) and (b).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **a current-carrying conductor** is placed in **a magnetic field**, this rule is used to identify **the direction of the force that is induced in the conductor.**
 
• The **magnetic field and the current's directions are opposed by the force that is induced in the conductor.**
 
• The** split ring acts as the commutator in an electric motor.** **After each half-rotation of the coil, the commutator changes the direction of the current flowing through the coil**.
 
• The coil keeps turning in the same direction as a result of this **current reversal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric motor**

 
 
• An **electromechanical device known as an electric motor transforms electrical energy into mechanical energy.**
 
• In other words, a motor is a device that generates **rotational force.**
 
• The interaction of the **magnetic and electric fields** is fundamental to how an electric motor operates.
 
• **Electric motors** can be divided into** two primary categories:**
 
 
• Both **AC and DC motors** fall under this category.
 
• While a DC motor uses direct current as its input, an AC motor uses alternating current.
